notes.body:
Based in Australia; came to know about MOHSYN through social media. Wants services for his parents, who live alone in DHA, Karachi, with his siblings living nearby.
Father, 83, has dementia, diabetes, cholesterol issues, vertigo, and occasional stomach pain. Mother, 74, is diabetic, has a lung condition that causes fatigue, and experiences stomach pain.
Parents already have a driver and domestic help and are expected to move to Creek Vista in 2–3 months. Client also requested shifting/relocation assistance.
Client initially wanted psychological support for his mother, with the psychologist introduced as a regular MOHSYN team member so that trust could gradually be built. He was informed that this would require cooperation from both MOHSYN and the family, and that the family would need to help the mother become comfortable with the services.
His main requirement was a dedicated and consistent FSO for his father, particularly because of his dementia. He wanted the same FSO to visit on consecutive days and even requested a visit one day before his mother's absence so his father could become familiar with the person.
He was repeatedly informed that MOHSYN cannot guarantee a dedicated FSO, the same FSO for every visit, or consecutive-day visits with the same FSO. A dedicated/fixed caretaker also could not be guaranteed.
He was also informed that his parents must be willing to receive MOHSYN services. MOHSYN can facilitate and make its best efforts, but the family would need to take responsibility for convincing and preparing the parents to accept the services.
Policy document and caretaker rates were shared. He also asked about invoices and was informed that MOHSYN provides online payment confirmation rather than a separate invoice in the format requested.
When he decided to subscribe, all the above limitations were reiterated. He subsequently informed us that he had arranged a live-in caretaker for his father, addressing his primary requirement for consistent care.

overviewSections.heading: Client Profile: Ms. Afroze Jehan & Mr. Tahir Siddiqui
overviewSections.body:
Location: Karachi
Benefactor: Yasir Siddique

overviewSections.heading: General Overview
overviewSections.body:
Ms. Afroze Jehan is a 68-year-old retired Montessori principal known for her compassionate nature and emotional strength. She became widowed in 2009. Despite managing osteoporosis, hypertension, and back problems, she remains active around the house and continues to play a central role in her family’s well-being. She enjoys reading Islamic literature and occasionally watching dramas in her leisure time.
Having endured significant personal losses, Ms. Jehan carries a quiet resilience and deep sense of responsibility, particularly toward her eldest son, Mr. Tahir Siddiqui, for whom she is the primary caretaker.
Mr. Tahir Siddiqui, aged 37, was diagnosed with Polymyositis during his university years. He has limited mobility and requires constant supervision, supported by three caretakers who work on rotation. Despite his physical limitations, he maintains an active and thoughtful disposition, spending much of his time writing articles and reflective pieces.
Ms Afroze has two other sons: the benefactor, Mr Yasir, and Mr Abdul Moez, who is based in KSA.

overviewSections.heading: Ms. Afroze Jehan
overviewSections.body:
- Suffers from osteoporosis, hypertension, and back pain.

- Experienced an accident that impacted her right lower side, resulting in ongoing mobility challenges.

- Was advised surgery at the time but chose not to undergo it.

- Maintains daily movement within the house to support her health and independence.

overviewSections.heading: Mr. Tahir Siddiqui
overviewSections.body:
- Diagnosis: Polymyositis (2009).

- 2016: Developed pneumonia; placed on ventilator for three days. Resulted in weakness and gradual inversion of the left lower leg.
2018: Underwent cholecystectomy and appendicectomy.
2023: Contracted COVID-19, leading to decreased lung function.
Prone to recurrent lung infections and requires preventive monitoring.
Mobility: Feet are non-functional; assisted daily by three rotating caretakers.

- Took 12 physio sessions from Dr Iqra.

overviewSections.heading: Dreamweaver Notes
overviewSections.body:
- Primary caretaker: Ms. Jehan closely monitors Tahir’s medical routine and daily comfort.

- Emotional landscape: She is deeply devoted yet experiences periodic anxiety regarding Tahir’s health and her family’s future, especially with her daughter-in-law’s upcoming relocation.

- Staff structure: The caretaker rotation is stable but should be checked periodically for quality and consistency.

overviewSections.heading: Psychologist Notes (Recommended)
overviewSections.body:
Miss Afroze Jehan is a remarkably composed, graceful, and lively woman whose personality reflects deep strength, emotional resilience, and an unwavering sense of purpose. Throughout her life, she has faced numerous challenges with courage and optimism. She takes immense pride in having raised her three children with exceptional care, dedication, and moral strength. Her two sons are successfully settled abroad as engineers, while her third son, despite being bedridden due to a severe physical condition, continues to work remotely a testament to the nurturing, motivation, and emotional encouragement provided by his mother.
Mis Afroze Jahan's life story is an inspiring journey of perseverance and unconditional love. Despite hardships and personal trials, she has remained strong, compassionate, and emotionally stable. She devotes her time and energy to caring for her ailing son, offering him companionship, motivation, and a sense of hope every day.
Beyond her caregiving role, she is a woman of refined taste and intellectual depth. She has a keen interest in literature, enjoys reading novels and poetry, and expresses her thoughts and life experiences in a beautifully articulate manner. Her conversations reflect wisdom, warmth, and emotional richness. Even at this stage of life, she remains organized, independent, and deeply connected with her family embodying resilience, grace, and the true spirit of motherhood.

overviewSections.heading: Overview
overviewSections.body:
From his location in the USA, Yousaf Majid coordinates support for his parents, Mr. Abdul Majid and Mrs. Majida Majid, and his brother, Mr. Jamal Majid, who live in Islamabad’s G-10/3 sector. The family has a long history in the United States, having lived there since the 1950s before returning to Pakistan in 1993. Due to previous experiences with property fraud in Islamabad, Mr. Abdul Majid is highly skeptical of service providers and requires formal written documentation and physical proof of credibility before fully engaging with new services.
The current focus of care is on medical recovery and household stability. Mr. Abdul Majid is recovering from a recent fall that resulted in a wrist fracture and is also managing stomach-related health issues. A doctor's visit has been scheduled to assess his recovery trajectory. While Mrs. Majida remains socially active, the brother, Jamal, is largely home-bound due to asthma and skin eczema. Per the benefactor’s instructions, interactions with Jamal are filtered, and all family communication is preferred during afternoon hours. The household is supported by a live-in driver and his wife, who provides domestic help.

Primary Care Utilization & Strategy:
Clinical Oversight: Scheduled doctor visits for fracture recovery and stomach condition monitoring.
Trust Building: Prioritizing delivery of formal brochures and documentation to address skepticism.
Engagement Schedule: Interaction restricted to afternoon hours based on family routine.
Emergency Contact: Mrs. Momina.

overviewSections.heading: Overview
overviewSections.body:
From his location in the USA, Mr. Ziad Asghar coordinates a structured support system for his 81-year-old mother, Mrs. Rabia Asghar, in Islamabad’s F-10/1 sector. Mrs. Rabia resides in her personal 2-kanal home with her daughter, Rizwana, and her family. The family has a background of international exposure, having been raised abroad while the late Mr. Asghar was associated with Caterpillar in the UAE. While the family operates as a well-coordinated support system—including another daughter, Lubna, who is a Vice Principal in F-8—they are currently looking to reduce their dependency on family members for medical logistics and transportation.
The primary focus of care is managing Mrs. Rabia’s significant mobility limitations; she can currently walk only 10 to 20 steps with assistance and relies on a walker or walking stick. Her existing wheelchair is non-functional and requires repair. To address these challenges and prepare for a potential knee replacement surgery scheduled for May or June, the immediate strategy involves onboarding urgent physiotherapy and providing assisted mobility for medical consultations. Despite her physical restrictions, Mrs. Rabia remains mentally active, maintains a strong interest in gardening, and prefers direct, personal communication with doctors.

overviewSections.heading: Line Facts: Asghar Family Profile
overviewSections.body:
- Beneficiary: Mrs. Rabia Asghar.

- Primary Benefactor: Mr. Ziad Asghar (USA).

- Location: House #26-A, Street #28, F-10/1, Islamabad (2 Kanal house).

- Onboarding/Assessment Date: April 11th, 2026.

-

overviewSections.heading: Health Profile
overviewSections.body:
- Mobility: Critically limited; walks 10–20 steps with assistance; high fatigue and fall risk.

- Conditions: Hypertension (on regular medication) and leg swelling.

- Upcoming Intervention: Knee replacement surgery under consideration for May–June.

- Household & Staff: Supported by a closely-knit family including daughters Rizwana (on-ground) and Lubna (secondary support); no dedicated driver is currently available.

-

overviewSections.heading: Identified Risks
overviewSections.body:
- Mobility (Critical): High risk of falls beyond short distances; current wheelchair is broken.

- Logistics Dependency: High reliance on family members (husband/son/daughter) for transportation to medical visits.

-

overviewSections.heading: Primary Care Utilization & Strategy
overviewSections.body:
- Clinical Support: Immediate onboarding of physiotherapy for pre-surgical conditioning.

- Medical Coordination: Facilitating dental appointments and assisted hospital visits.

- Equipment Maintenance: Repairing the existing wheelchair to enable safe movement.

- Engagement Style: Direct interaction with the beneficiary; preference for female team members during visits.

- Emergency Contacts: Ms. Rizwana Asghar and Ms. Lubna Asghar.

overviewSections.heading: Client Profile: Miss Faryda
overviewSections.body: Location: Bahria Enclave, Islamabad

overviewSections.heading: General Overview
overviewSections.body:
Miss Faryda is a highly independent and strong-willed individual who lives alone in Bahria Enclave, Islamabad. She leads an active lifestyle and places great importance on maintaining her personal space, daily routines, and individual preferences. She values consistency, autonomy, and respectful support that aligns with the way she chooses to live.
Her cat is an integral part of her home life and provides significant companionship and emotional comfort. Miss Faryda shares a close bond with her daughter, Zaiena, while her son, Zohare, resides in Dubai and actively supports her needs from abroad.
A creative individual, Miss Faryda has dedicated part of her home to her crafting hobbies. She has a particular passion for bat-themed creations and doll-making, reflecting her artistic personality and attention to detail.
Through her interactions with Mohsyn, Miss Faryda has consistently demonstrated high standards and an appreciation for reliability, professionalism, and continuity of care. She responds best to caregivers who respect her independence, communicate clearly, and understand her established routines and preferences.

overviewSections.heading: 1. Intake Summary & Client Disposition
overviewSections.body:
- Client Background: The sponsor, Zohra, reached out from Buffalo, NY, after viewing a reel by Junaid Akram. She is an only child; her father passed away when she was three years old. He was a supervisor at Saudi Airlines and retired 10 years ago.

- Sponsor Disposition: During the initial conversation, Zohra expressed hesitation and trust issues regarding Field Service Officers (FSOs) visiting her mother’s residence. After a detailed explanation of our operational security and care protocols, she felt reassured and satisfied.

- Current Status: She is very interested in the service setup but requested time to consult with her mother first before confirming onboarding.

overviewSections.heading: Primary Patient: Hajra Begum (Age: 60+)
overviewSections.body:
- Medical Landscape: Diagnosed with Hypertension, Arthritis, and Osteoporosis.

- Mobility Restrictions & Fall History: Arthritis has significantly limited her physical mobility. She has a history of two falls, one resulting in a broken wrist bone.

- Support System: Relatives are considered unreliable. Informal assistance is occasionally provided by a few local friends of her daughter who drop in to check on her.

overviewSections.heading: 3. Domestic Dynamic & Access Constraints
overviewSections.body:
- Property Layout: The ground floor of the property is rented out to a commercial bank; Hajra Begum resides on the 1st floor.

- Domestic Privacy Boundaries: The patient leads a very private life and strictly opposes outside staff or strangers entering her residential space.

- Meeting Protocol: If operational staff or care managers need to conduct in-person discussions, meetings must take place downstairs in the bank area on the ground floor. No in-home entry is permitted.

overviewSections.heading: Operational Boundary Directive: Outdoor Assistance Only
overviewSections.body: Deliverables for this case are strictly limited to outdoor errands and off-site support (e.g., grocery procurement, utility bill payments, pharmacy pickups, and external logistics). Field personnel must not request or attempt entry into the 1st-floor residence.

overviewSections.heading: 4. Proposed Scope of Care & Services
overviewSections.body:
- Outdoor Errand & Logistical Facilitation: Manage all routine external tasks and errands to prevent the mother from taking unnecessary physical risks or exertion.

- Off-Site Care Coordination: Provide remote health check-ins, medication reminders, and appointment scheduling via direct phone/WhatsApp updates.

overviewSections.heading: 5. Immediate Operational Next Steps
overviewSections.body:
- Follow-Up: Await an update from Zohra following her conversation with her mother.

- Service Plan Customization: Prepare an outdoor-focused service agreement that respects domestic entry boundaries.

- Field Team Briefing: Ensure the local Karachi operational team is briefed regarding the ground-floor bank meeting protocol for initial consultations.
